clue.text: Leader of society amongst Macs not hybridised!

definitions.text: Leader of society amongst Macs not hybridised!

indicators.note: amongst says the one letter is placed among the mixed letters
hybridised means crossed and mixed, so the letters of these words are blended into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from society

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a prominent person is found among Macs of pure, unmixed stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybridised' turns MACS NOT into SCOTMAN, and 'amongst' puts S, the leader of 'society', inside it. As a whole the clue describes the answer: Macs are Scots, and one leading society among them is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Surnames beginning Mac are typically Scottish, so a pure-blooded Mac is a man from Scotland.

clue.text: The main picture?

parts.note: 'the main' is an old poetic name for the ocean, so a picture of the main is a painting of the ocean view

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' reads as 'chief', but in poetry 'the main' is the open sea, so this is a painting of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting showing a view of the ocean is a marine picture, which is what 'the main' (the sea) gives.

clue.text: Girl, in a month, may come to make too much of the part

definitions.text: make too much of the part

indicators.note: in says the girl's name is placed inside the month

parts.note: OCT is the short form of October
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman may, within a month, start overplaying her stage role.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo a stage role is to exaggerate the acting of it, making too much of it.

clue.text: Musical instrument is taken up by sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read upwards, so is is reversed

parts.note: a tar is an old name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is picked up and carried off by a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns IS into SI in this down clue; 'by' puts TAR beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked stringed instrument of Indian classical music.

clue.text: Barbara lewdly embraces a scoundrel — it has a magical effect!

indicators.note: embraces says the mixed name wraps around the other pieces
lewdly suggests loose, disordered behaviour, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A woman named Barbara indecently hugs a rogue, which has quite an effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lewdly' is the anagram signal on the name and 'embraces' the container signal; the definition is the exclamation at the end, a conjuror's word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the classic incantation spoken by conjurors, a word supposed to work magic.

clue.text: Achilles' mother is following the Cross?

indicators.note: following means is comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a cross is shaped like the letter T

explanation.surface: A question whether the mother of Achilles is walking behind a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' signals that 'is' comes last. Thetis was the sea-nymph of Greek myth who dipped her son Achilles in the Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the sea-nymph Thetis bore the hero Achilles to the mortal Peleus.

clue.text: Game for nimble feet hard work on the booze

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first pieces sit above the next

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
op, short for opus, is a work
Scotch whisky is booze

explanation.surface: A game needing quick feet is hard going after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts H and OP above SCOTCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares, needing agile footwork.

clue.text: Excavation producing cash for me?

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
something meant for me is mine

explanation.surface: Digging that turns up money for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit or shaft dug to extract an ore is a kind of excavation.

clue.text: Holy man doing well, as it were, to take a walk

parts.note: ST, saint, is a holy man
someone doing well is said to be on a roll

explanation.surface: A saint enjoying good fortune goes for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' marks the idiom: someone on a run of success is 'on a roll'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely, unhurried walk is a stroll, and to take one is to amble.

clue.text: A fresh medical treatment without need for initial opening?

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky, impudent

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word for treatment is not needed and is dropped

parts.note: a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: Asking whether a new medical procedure no longer needs a first incision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without need for initial' drops the C of CURE to leave URE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, such as a camera's lens opening.

clue.text: Batsman with single run, needing to have put in training

indicators.note: says the training letters are placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: single means one
PE is physical education, training
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricketer who scored one run needs more practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have put in' is the container signal. In cricket the opening batsmen go in first; 'Batsman' looks like part of the surface story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the two batsmen who start the innings are called the openers.

clue.text: hold meeting

clue.text: Group sharing beliefs of ailing former politician

parts.note: a church is a body of people sharing one faith
ailing means ill

explanation.surface: A congregation of sick people, or the faith of an old statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Winston Churchill was British prime minister during the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was a British statesman, wartime prime minister, now historical.

clue.text: One in variety of a naval blue is not for sale?

indicators.note: in says the single letter is placed inside the mixed letters
a variety of the letters is a different arrangement of them

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A single shade among a range of navy blues cannot be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges A NAVAL BLUE, and 'in' puts I (one) inside to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that cannot be obtained or bought are out of stock, not on offer.

clue.text: Confrontation between tars?

parts.note: tars are sailors, but also tarred things; pitch is tar, so a fight between pitched things is a set-piece fight

explanation.walkthrough: Tars are sailors, but pitch is tar, so things coated in tar are 'pitched': a fight between them is a set-piece fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-piece clash between armies drawn up in position is a full-scale fight.

clue.text: Longing for anger in HK to dissipate

indicators.note: dissipate means scatter, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A wish for rage in Hong Kong to fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: HK is the abbreviation for Hong Kong.
explanation.definitionFit: A hankering is a yearning or strong desire, the same as a longing.

clue.text: Christian, say, in the Christian era, taking this position over New Testament

indicators.note: taking means the era is joined by the next piece
in a down clue, over means the pieces stand above New Testament

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the Christian era
here is this position
NT is New Testament

explanation.surface: A believer of the Christian era is placed here above the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue puts HERE above NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian is an example of a follower, a supporter of a faith.

clue.text: Depend upon something uncertain to put the baubles on the tree?

definitions.meaning: to be in a precarious state with success or failure at stake

definitions.text: to put the baubles on the tree?
definitions.meaning: decorations are hung on the Christmas tree from a loop of cotton

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: baubles are hung on a Christmas tree on loops of cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be in a precarious state, while literally it describes ornaments dangling on cotton.

clue.text: Girl's individual about foremost in intrepidity — this one?

definitions.text: Girl's individual about foremost in intrepidity — this one?

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl

indicators.note: about says the word for individual goes around the next letter

parts.note: one is an individual

indicators.note: foremost in picks out the first letter of intrepidity

explanation.surface: Asking whether a girl, uniquely brave, is a female champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ONE around I, the first letter of 'intrepidity'. As a whole, the clue describes a brave female.
explanation.definitionFit: A female known for courage, the leading lady of bravery, is a female hero.

clue.text: Put money away after rise? I have, trying to avoid tax, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise turns the word upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to save is to put money away
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Banking cash after a pay rise, someone claims to dodge tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after rise' is the reversal signal, a rise turning the word upwards in this down clue. Tax avoidance is an example of dodging, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone avoiding a tax or a question is dodging, being slippery, like a tax evader.

clue.text: Good idea gets cry of glee and zeal? Not half

parts.note: whee is a cry of delight

indicators.note: not half means only half of zeal is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A bright plan earns a whoop of delight and enthusiasm, though not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps ZE, the first half of 'zeal'. A wheeze is British slang for a clever scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is British slang for a clever scheme or trick.

clue.text: the rush

clue.text: Another answer holds this reversed word meaning 'trap'

indicators.note: reversed means the run is read backwards
holds means the run of letters sits inside the words another answer

explanation.surface: A clue pointing to another entry that contains a word for a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' points to ERANS spanning 'anothER ANSwer', and 'reversed' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a noose or device for catching animals, so it is a trap.

clue.text: Most excellent drug gives you a fixed expression

parts.note: a star is the best, most excellent performer
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A top-quality narcotic leaves the user looking glassy.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for ecstasy. 'Fixed expression' looks like an idiom, but here it is a fixed gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A stare is a fixed gaze, an unmoving look on the face.

clue.text: Extract a bit of evidence following legal process

indicators.note: a bit of the word evidence here is its first letter

parts.note: licit means lawful, legal

explanation.surface: A fragment of proof is drawn out in court proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' takes E from 'evidence'; LICIT means lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out information or a response, to extract it.

clue.text: Causing irritation, as I have snatched an item of lingerie

indicators.note: snatched means the other pieces grab and hold the lingerie inside them

parts.note: a bra is an item of lingerie
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone's theft of underwear is causing annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snatched' is the container signal: the lingerie item goes inside the other pieces, just after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive rubs harshly and grates, causing annoyance.

clue.text: Say soldiers in retreat appear

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Troops falling back come into view, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns EG REME backwards. REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come into view, to appear.

clue.text: Respectful and always filling a gap

indicators.note: filling says the word for always is placed inside the gap

parts.note: a rent is a tear or gap
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone polite who is forever plugging holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' is the container signal; a rent is a tear in cloth, a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reverent means showing deep respect or devotion.
